subtitle: Daily factory metrics from local pi transcripts, kaizen reporters, GitHub, tasks, and git.
score: Each category has one key metric, marked in red. Optimize three: tasks completed (up), cost per merged PR counting all spend (down), and operator messages per merged PR (down). Hold three as guardrails, so the optimized metrics cannot improve through worse work: escaped defects per merged PR, lines rewritten within 21 days, and subagent failures. PR counts are not a target, because splitting work raises them without adding value. The last 7 days are compared with the prior 7 days. Sparklines span the whole period: the red dot is the latest value and the black dot is the maximum. Green or red marks a change of 10% or more, for better or worse.
opened: PRs authored by the operator's configured GitHub logins, by creation day. Agent-opened PRs use those logins, so this counts agent and hand-made PRs together. Only transcript-linked PRs are discoverable.
merged: PRs merged per day. Bursts can be stacks landing together.
landed: Merged PRs by merge day. A merged PR counts as landed after 7 days with no revert and no fix: PR that names it (fixes #N, follow-up to #N, regression from #N). Red marks PRs named by a fix: PR within 7 days. Grey marks PRs still inside their 7-day window. A fix that does not name the PR goes undetected.
tasks: Tasks from the supplied task file, by completion day. A task is landed when every PR linked to it (task id in the PR title, branch, or body) landed. Tasks with no linked PR are counted separately. Tasks whose PRs are still open or in the 7-day window are holding.
abandoned: PRs closed without merging, by close day, and their direct cost: the cost of the sessions that worked on them.
queue: Tasks at the end of each day: not started (queue) and started but not done (in progress). Open PRs is the count of PRs open at the end of the day.
cpp: Three ways to price a merged PR. All spend: every dollar spent in the last 7 days divided by the PRs merged in those days, so it includes overhead such as planning, kaizen, and factory work. Product repos: the same, counting only sessions in product repos. Direct: the cost of the sessions that worked on that PR (the session that opened it, sessions that touched it, and their subagents). A session that worked on several PRs splits its cost evenly across them. The red line is the 7-day median of direct cost. Each grey dot is one PR.
spend: Provider-reported cost of every pi session and subagent run, by the directory the session ran in. Session classes come from local configuration.
cw: Cost of writing the prompt cache, as a share of all spend, 7-day. Cache writes are the largest cost line.
longc: Share of spend on turns that carried more than 150k tokens of context, 7-day.
coverage: Share of spend, over 7 days, in sessions that worked on at least one PR. A session worked on a PR if it opened the PR or named it in a gh pr command or a PR-tracker call. The rest is planning, factory work, kaizen, and sessions with no detected PR.
repo_cost: Direct cost per merged PR, by repo. Direct cost is the cost of the sessions that worked on the PR. The dot marks the median and the line runs to the 90th percentile. Only repos with at least 5 merged PRs appear.
loops: Review-loop spend by round over the whole period.
rewrites: Cache rewrites by cause over the whole period. Idle means the session paused longer than the cache lifetime.
nocollector_cloud: Cloud runs do not report cost to a local source yet. Supply an extension tile.
nocollector_review: Review dispatchers do not report cost to a local source yet. Supply an extension tile.
ops_pr: Messages the operator typed, including the first prompt as defined by operator-signals, divided by PRs merged, 7-day. Lower means fewer touches per PR.
touches: Operator touches per day by type. Corrections, aborts, approvals, and status checks use the kaizen operator-signals rules. Other covers answers, instructions, and new requests. The line is reviews left on the operator's PRs by other people.
fr_pr: Rows agents wrote to friction.md when someone sent their work back, divided by PRs merged, 7-day.
catcher: Friction rows by who caught the problem. Free-text values are normalized to five.
escaped: Friction rows caught by the operator or CI per merged PR, over 7 days. Each is a defect that got past the agent's own checks and review.
decisions: Decisions agents settled on their own and logged in open-questions.md. Reversed share is the share of judged entries the operator reversed, 14-day. Judged share is the share of entries that got any verdict.
htm: Hours from PR creation to merge. Dots are single PRs, the line is the 7-day median.
timesplit: Wall time across all main sessions, by who held the turn.
funnel: Review-loop rounds over the whole period. The dark part of each bar is rounds where a reviewer blocked.
firstclean: Share of coder runs whose first review did not block, by coder model. The two models got different work.
rework: Merged PRs by merge week: share with no commits pushed after opening, no changes requested, and passing final checks.
hdispatch: Verdicts from the review dispatcher against what happened next. Changed means commits landed after the reviewed commit.
churn: churn21 counts deleted lines whose first-parent origin landed within 21 days before the deleting change, divided by lines added. Moved is the share of added lines that git blame -M -C traces to older code. Revisit is the share of changes that touch a file changed in the previous 7 days.
churn_chart: All configured repos, 7-day window. Deleted lines originated within 21 days divided by added lines. See the churn table for exclusions.
failures: Subagent runs that failed, timed out, or needed attention, per day. Red is pr-babysitter. Zero-duration failed runs never started and are annotated separately.
guards: Commands blocked by the autonomy guard or the harness, per day.
automations: Automation runs per day. Supply an extension collector.
commits: First-parent commits landed in the configured factory checkouts.
kaizen: Findings per kaizen and hansei run. Kaizen states come from each findings file.
nocollector_effective: Days from a finding's first run to its effective verdict. Needs two more kaizen runs that re-check landed fixes.
schema: Share of friction rows whose caught-by value is one of the five allowed values, 7-day. Agents write it as free text, so this page normalizes it.
notes: Spend is the provider-reported usage.cost.total on each assistant message in pi sessions, across main sessions and subagent runs, by message date. Copies under subagent-artifacts/ are skipped because they duplicate subagent runs.
Only local pi session spend is counted. Missing sources leave null fields. PR series cover successfully read PRs; missing PRs and unavailable hosts appear in the coverage note.
Subagents take their parent session's class. A session's window cost, with its subagents, is split evenly over the PRs it links.

Landed counts only explicit references: a revert, or a fix: PR whose title or body says it fixes, follows up on, or reverts the PR. Matching on shared files is not used. Unnamed or undiscovered fixes go undetected.
Prompts, responses, and transcript text are not on this page.
cloud: Cloud runs do not report cost to a local source yet. Supply an extension tile.
revcost: Review dispatchers do not report cost to a local source yet. Supply an extension tile.
effective: Days from a finding's first run to its effective verdict. Needs two more kaizen runs that re-check landed fixes.
churn_tbl: churn21 counts deleted lines whose first-parent origin landed within 21 days before the deleting change, divided by lines added. Moved is the share of added lines that git blame -M -C traces to older code. Revisit is the share of changes that touch a file changed in the previous 7 days.
